label: Corruptible / incorruptible
term: corruptible / incorruptible (simply, or in a respect)
resolution: In Metaph. IX, lect. 9 n. 4 distinguishes being corruptible simply (able to fail to be in substance) from being corruptible in a respect (able to fail to be in a place, quantity or quality). The case keeps one primitive, CanFailToBe x r, and reads 'simply' as its instance at r = esse (IncorruptibleSimply). STMT-EVERY-POTENCY-IS-OF-CONTRADICTION is per respect: potency in r gives corruptibility in r only. STMT-INCORRUPTIBLE-PRIOR-IN-SUBSTANCE-TO-CORRUPTIBLE and STMT-INCORRUPTIBLE-IS-IN-ACT-IN-SUBSTANCE use the simple sense only. The argument never passes from a potency in an accidental respect to simple corruptibility; that passage is exactly what n. 6 forbids (nihil prohibet, id quod est incorruptibile simpliciter, esse in potentia secundum quid), and the countermodel of ActPriorFromIncorruptibleFacts item 6 is a being incorruptible simply and in potency, hence able to fail to be, in a respect other than substance.
